entries.subject: Stars in the picture
entries.finding: The picture was first cleaned only by the bake's pass over the Gaia foreground stars, which leaves the brightest stars, the faint ones Gaia cannot certify and those it reads as extended. The Nebula Lab's NOX removes them all and keeps the galaxy's arms and dust lanes; it also takes the galaxy's own compact knots and clusters, most visibly in M51, which was looked at and accepted on 2026-10-03; 13 of the 13 Gaia stars brighter than G 14 in the picture had a glow, filled out to at most 124 px (39″). The lab's isophote fill, made for ellipticals, left a dark notch on a spiral, so the glow is filled from the ring around it.

entries.subject: Catalogued objects as dots
entries.finding: 4,351 dots from 3 published tables: 4,202 hii region candidates (Rousseau-Nepton et al. (2018), CDS J/MNRAS/477/4152, 4,285 rows in the file); 139 planetary nebulae (Scheuermann et al. (2022), CDS J/MNRAS/511/6087, 1,049 rows in the file); 10 supernova remnants (Scheuermann et al. (2022), CDS J/MNRAS/511/6087, 1,049 rows in the file). Each dot is a catalogued object at its published sky position, placed where its sight line meets the disc. Its height above the disc is drawn from a 438 pc layer, the scale length over 7.3 ([Kregel et al. 2002](https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0204154), [record](../../sources/kregel-2002-disc-flattening.json)); that height is not measured.
